flawed_step: 0035–0036: The proof claims that every nonempty C_ij equals δ(S_i) and is itself a cut-set. In general, S_i may have edges to several components T_j, so δ(S_i) is the union of multiple C_ij sets, not one C_ij.
counterexample: Let G be the 4-cycle with V={s1,t1,s2,t2} and E={s1t1,t1s2,s2t2,t2s1}. Take S={s1,s2} and T={t1,t2}. The components of G[S] are S1={s1}, S2={s2}, and those of G[T] are T1={t1}, T2={t2}. Then C11={s1t1} is nonempty, but δ(S1)={s1t1,s1t2}, so C11≠δ(S1). Moreover, C11 is not a cut-set: deleting the single edge s1t1 leaves the path s1-t2-s2-t1, so the connected graph remains connected. Equivalently, no nontrivial vertex partition of a 4-cycle has exactly one crossing edge. Thus C11 is not a minimal cut.
assessment_summary: Steps 1 and 2 correctly partition the original cut into the disjoint component-pair edge sets C_ij. The first definitive failure is Step 3: an individual nonempty C_ij need not be a cut at all, as the explicit 4-cycle demonstrates. Hence the proposed decomposition is not established.
